glance: Happy Thanksgiving: US stock and bond markets were closed today; stocks reopen Friday for a half-day session ending at noon CT.
Bitcoin climbed to about $61,000 on Thanksgiving, squeezing short sellers in thin holiday trading.
Reports say Pentagon officials floated a wartime law to pressure Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang; Huang testifies to Congress next week.
1Password disclosed a breach of internal systems via an employee's GitHub account; customer vaults were not touched.
Israeli strikes killed at least eight people in Gaza on Thursday, including a Hamas-appointed deputy minister, local officials say.

tech.headline: Pentagon reportedly weighed wartime law to put Huang back atop Nvidia
tech.summary: The Washington Post reports Pentagon officials discussed invoking the Defense Production Act to press Nvidia's board into reappointing Jensen Huang as CEO. Reuters separately reports the Justice Department never opened a formal probe into Huang before he was cleared, and the WSJ says officials told Congress there is no evidence China orchestrated the relationship at the center of the scandal. The episode is raising sharp questions about government pressure on a private company's board; Huang is due to testify before Congress next week.

tech.headline: 1Password says hackers got into its internal systems
tech.summary: Password manager 1Password disclosed that attackers broke in through a compromised employee GitHub account and took customer names and email addresses. The company says encrypted vault contents and passwords were not accessed. Users should still watch for targeted phishing that uses the stolen contact details.

tech.headline: FCC clears SpaceX for up to 1 million data-center satellites
tech.summary: US regulators authorized SpaceX to deploy as many as 1 million satellites intended to host AI computing in orbit, an enormous jump from today's Starlink fleet. The approval lands as Tesla and SpaceX reportedly explore an all-stock merger valuing the pair near $3.5 trillion, which would combine Musk's rocket, satellite and AI businesses with the carmaker.

tech.headline: Banned Nvidia chips still on offer in China; Nvidia settles old investor suit
tech.summary: The Washington Post found top-end Nvidia servers still being quoted in Shenzhen despite US export bans, with B300 systems priced above $3 million, underscoring how hard the controls are to enforce. Separately, Reuters reports Nvidia agreed to pay $290 million to settle a 2018 class action over how it disclosed crypto-mining demand for its GPUs. Nvidia shares fell about 4% Wednesday.

tech.headline: States move against AI toys and Character.AI's data sale
tech.summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on AI chatbot toys just as holiday shopping begins. Meanwhile, 42 state attorneys general are opposing Character.AI's plan to auction data from more than 21 million US accounts, including over 2 million registered to minors.

tech.headline: OpenAI claims a result on a classic math problem
tech.summary: OpenAI posted a preprint arguing that the exponent governing how fast matrices can be multiplied is exactly 9/4, which would settle a long-open question in computer science if it holds up. Outside mathematicians have yet to verify the proof, but it is the boldest claim yet of AI-assisted research producing a major theoretical result.

tech.headline: ElevenLabs eyes $33 billion valuation
tech.summary: Bloomberg reports voice-AI startup ElevenLabs is in early talks for a 2027 funding round targeting a $33 billion valuation, up from $22 billion in September, a sign investor appetite for AI apps remains strong even as chip stocks wobble.

markets.asOf: market close, Nov 25 for stocks, yield and oil; bitcoin late afternoon Nov 26. US markets closed today for Thanksgiving
markets.summary: US stock and bond markets were closed for Thanksgiving and reopen Friday for a shortened session; bitcoin rose toward $61,000 in thin holiday trading.

other.headline: Hot inflation sets up a likely December Fed hike
other.summary: October's PCE price index rose 3.8% from a year earlier, the most since 2023, with core prices up 3.3%, and third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%. Futures now price roughly a 97% chance of a quarter-point rate increase next month.

other.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least eight in Gaza
other.summary: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed at least eight people on Thursday, among them a Hamas-appointed deputy minister, according to local officials, adding strain to the fragile ceasefire. Separately, Iran's government has vowed to use every available tool against the US naval blockade, keeping Gulf tensions in focus.

other.headline: New tariffs proposed on 14 trading partners
other.summary: The administration proposed duties of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 others over excess factory capacity, layered on existing tariffs. They would follow hearings and public comment, likely January at the earliest; the US-China trade truce expires Jan. 10.

other.headline: Busy holiday travel, and the 100th Macy's parade
other.summary: AAA expected more than 81 million Americans to travel over the holiday, slightly below last year's record amid high airfares and gas prices. The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade marked its 100th edition Thursday morning in New York.

other.headline: Record online holiday spending forecast as deals begin
other.summary: Adobe projects US online holiday sales will reach a record $275.1 billion, up 6.7% from last year, with Thanksgiving, Black Friday and Cyber Monday the peak days for discounts.

other.headline: Neuralink cleared for pivotal ALS implant trial
other.summary: Neuralink says the FDA approved a pivotal trial of its brain-computer implant in people with ALS, a key step toward potential market approval of the device.
